E-Commerce Marketplace Orders
& Delivery Dashboard

Abstract
•  Olist marketplace orders span 2016–2018.
•  Nine CSV files feed a normalized MySQL database.
•  Ten SQL reports explain orders, revenue and delivery.
•  A custom local website provides filters and order details.
•  Charts, exact values and exports support review.
•  A five-minute cache speeds repeated requests.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
Introduction
•  Marketplace records span several related files.
•  Manual joins make analysis slow and inconsistent.
•  Operations users need delivery and revenue comparisons.
•  Objectives: clean data, enforce keys and build ten reports.
•  The dashboard connects report results to filters and exports.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
Scope and Methodology
•  Historical Brazilian orders, payments, deliveries and reviews.
•  Analytics uses MySQL queries against the imported dataset.
•  The project excludes checkout and real-time processing.
•  Inspect, clean and import source files.
•  Validate SQL results, then present charts and exports.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
Problem Identification and Analysis
•  Nine linked CSV files complicate consistent analysis.
•  Geolocation repeats zip prefixes. Review identifiers may repeat.
•  Undelivered orders can have missing delivery dates.
•  Operations users need state, timing and revenue comparisons.
•  Normalized storage supports consistent joins and constraints.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
Solution Design and Implementation
•  Schema and repeatable CSV import.
•  SQL views and ten parameterized report queries.
•  Python HTTP endpoints validate filters and query MySQL.
•  HTML, CSS and JavaScript render the custom website.
•  A bounded cache reuses identical requests for five minutes.
Template: CAPSTONE PP TEMPLATE.pdf. Source content: CAPSTONE REVIEW 1.pptx. Project updates verified against current SQL and WEBPAGE files and local MySQL results. Dataset period: 2016–2018.
System Architecture
•  Data source: nine Olist CSV files
•  Storage: nine normalized MySQL tables
•  Analysis: two views and ten report queries
•  Service: Python HTTP server with in-memory cache
•  Interface: Overview, Orders, Reports and Database
•  Output: charts, exact values, CSV, Excel and PDF

Module 1: Dataset and Database
•  Owner: Monish L, 1972260035
•  Clean blanks and convert types.
•  Aggregate geolocation by zip prefix.
•  Separate customers, orders, items, payments and reviews.
•  Load in foreign-key order and validate constraints.

Module 1: Schema and Data Evidence
•  Orders: 99,441 records
•  Order items: 112,650 records
•  Payments: 103,886 records
•  Products: 32,951 records
•  Primary and foreign keys connect normalized tables.

Module 2: SQL and Report Engine
•  Owner: Prasannakumar S, 1924260035
•  Join related entities through relational keys.
•  Use aggregation, CASE, views and ranking queries.
•  Pass filters separately from SQL text.
•  Reuse report results for charts, exact values and exports.

Module 2: Query and Actual Output
•  R10 groups reviews by delivery outcome.
•  On time: 4.29 / 5 across 88,658 reviews.
•  Late: 2.57 / 5 across 7,701 reviews.
•  Late deliveries have lower average reviews in this dataset.
•  This comparison shows association, not causation.

Module 3: Website and Dashboard
•  Owner: S Hari Surendran, 1912260615
•  Overview presents marketplace KPIs and delivery outcomes.
•  Orders supports identifier search, pagination and details.
•  Reports provides ten distinct charts, exact values and exports.
•  Database explains columns, relationships and views.

Module 3: Interface and Implementation
•  Frontend: HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
•  Backend: Python HTTP server with MySQL access.
•  Date shortcuts cover 2016, 2017 and 2018.
•  Full state names improve readability.
•  The original Streamlit app remains in WEBPAGE/app.

Report Visualizations

•  R03 Top states: ranked bars
•  R04 Payment shares: waffle chart
•  R05 Monthly delivery time: area chart
•  R06 On-time versus late: grouped bars
•  R07 Category revenue: treemap
•  R08 Freight by state: lollipop chart
•  R09 Delivery distribution: histogram
•  R10 Review scores: five-star ratings

Report Interaction and Exports
•  Select a chart element to inspect exact values.
•  Partial stars show fractional review scores.
•  Keyboard controls support chart exploration.
•  CSV, Excel and PDF exports use the report engine.
•  Each filter combination has a separate cache entry.

Integration of Modules
•  Module 1 supplies cleaned records and validated relationships.
•  Module 2 produces filtered report results.
•  Module 3 displays results as charts and tables.
•  R07 ranks category revenue and renders a treemap.
•  SQL and WEBPAGE folders separate database and app source.

Results and Discussion
•  Orders: 99,441
•  Item revenue: R$13,591,643.70
•  Average delivery time: 12.50 days
•  Average review: 4.09 / 5
•  São Paulo accounts for 41,731 orders.
•  Historical Olist data has defined coverage limits.

Learning and Personal Development
•  Monish: relational keys, cleaning and normalization.
•  Prasannakumar: joins, views and ranking queries.
•  Hari: APIs, chart interactions and report exports.
•  Date-format repairs restored monthly trends.
•  Caching reduces repeated database work.

Conclusion
•  The project connects historical marketplace data to MySQL.
•  The custom dashboard supports operational analysis.
•  Ten reports have distinct graphical representations.
•  Exact values and exports support traceable results.
•  Future work includes saved filters and report scheduling.
